cases.name: Karen Elise Pulley
cases.about: She was studying to become a paralegal at Chattanooga State. Lisette Monroe’s sweet words describing her sister: "She was an angel on loan from Heaven. Very gentle, quiet spirit. sweet, happy, and loved the Lord, Jesus, with all her heart."
cases.narrative:
He parked near a house in the Brainerd area of Chattanooga where she lived with two female house mates. Nichols watched the house from outside and saw one of the women dress and leave. He armed himself with a short length of two-by-four lumber, climbed in a bathroom window, and roamed through the house. When he found Karen in bed and alone, he struck her in the head with the two-by-four, tore her clothes from her, and forcibly raped her vaginally. Afterwards, Nichols hit her in the head several more times with the two-by-four, crushing her skull, and left her on the floor, bleeding and unconscious. Nichols inflicted an astounding amount of damage to Karen Pulley’s head and body, as is evident from both the autopsy and the gruesome crime-scene photos.

One of Pulley’s house mates found her the next morning, alive but unconscious, lying on the floor in a large pool of blood. Karen died at the hospital later that day — she never regained consciousness.

cases.name: Ellen Wilson McKenzie
cases.about: "Ellen was a very private person," friend Angela Terry said. "She kept to herself. But now, if you were her friend, you were her friend for life. She would do anything for you." Ellen often helped others, praying with them or offering advice. Friends said she struggled with depression.

cases.name: Kara Akins
cases.about: The family of Kara Akins released a statement saying the mother of 7 was "known for her compassion, Kara frequently engaged in acts of kindness that touched the lives of others." Akins was a mother to seven — aged 29 to 6 — and a dedicated community advocate, family members told the Chattanooga Times Free Press. She volunteered, took foster children into her home and went out of her way to help members of Chattanooga's homeless community, they said.
cases.narrative: On 11/29/2023, she was found dead at a residence in Chattanooga, TN. Akins died of homicide by manual strangulation and a blunt force head injury, according to the medical examiner's report. The report describes bruises and scratches around her face, jaw and neck.

cases.name: Brooke Killings
cases.about:
Killings' sister, Hannah Williams says the two were 'super close' when they were younger.

"She used to always dress me up and, you know, put those beaded necklaces around me and everything, and did my hair all the time," Williams said. "I was really close with her out of all of my other siblings."
It was a bond that Williams says she maintained even after Killings enlisted in the Army, where she served for 11 years, including overseas in Kuwait and Afghanistan, achieving the rank of staff sergeant.

Williams says that service "shaped her into the person that she was."

"We talked. You know, she was in there for 11 years, but we were close. We talked. Tried to talk every day." Even though Killings was only 5' 2", Williams says she was "strong as an ox," and "would do absolutely anything for her family and her kids."

Despite the news, Hannah says she will remember her sister one way and one way only: as her best friend who always knew the right thing to say.

"She would always keep me in my right mind and give me good advice about things."
cases.narrative: On 8/21/2024, Chattanooga police found her body in the woods off Interstate 75 in Catoosa County, GA. Prosecutors accused Napier of shooting Killings at his house before he dumped her body in duct-taped trash bags. Police say Napier shot Brooke Killings just below her eye, killing her.
